kjv: they pierced my hands and my feet (KJV 22:16)
mine: like a lion they are at my hands and my feet
note: the Masoretic text reads ka'ari "like a lion"; the LXX (oryxan "they dug"), Syriac, Vulgate and a Nahal Hever manuscript (k'rw) point to a verb ("they bored/pierced"); the KJV follows that tradition, central to Christian reading of the crucifixion, while I translate the WLC as printed.

kjv: my darling from the power of the dog (KJV 22:20)
mine: my precious life from the power of the dog
note: yehidati "my only one" = my unique life (parallel "my soul"); "darling" now means a loved person.

kjv: from the horns of the unicorns (KJV 22:21)
mine: From the horns of the wild oxen
note: re'emim are wild oxen (cf. Job 39:9); and 'anitani is "you have answered me", a sudden turn from lament to thanks that the KJV's "thou hast heard me" partly preserves.
